proposal.claim:
ORIGIN. reports/SCOUT.jsonl line 10, slug `binance-leveraged-token-hedge-basket-restore-mandated-leverage`, confidence high. This is NOT the line H0017 and H0019 took. That line, slug `leveraged-binance-usd-m-perpetual-short-whose-collateral`, has now been read three times -- cci_breakout, cci_reversion, cci_mtf -- and both registrations closed. This line's own `distinct_from` field says the payer is "a product-level hedge portfolio obeying a leverage mandate, not a funding-paying long, a liquidated trader, or any payer already in the notebook", which names exactly the two payers this ledger has already spent 234 rows on.

WHO IS STRUCTURALLY PAYING, AND WHY THEY KEEP DOING IT. A Binance Leveraged Token is not a token; it is a claim on a basket of USD-M perpetual positions carrying a mandated leverage. When the underlying moves, the basket's realised leverage drifts off the mandate, and the mandate is restored by trading the perpetual in the SAME direction as the move that broke it: buying more exposure after a favourable move, cutting it after an adverse one. The basket does not choose whether to trade, does not choose when, and does not get to decline because the spread is wide -- restoring the ratio is the product, and a leveraged token that stops restoring it is no longer the instrument its holders bought. The scout line states the mandate compels "same-direction trading after sufficiently large moves regardless of execution cost", and names what would end it: discontinuation of the product, removal of the perpetual from the basket, or replacement of the leverage-restoration mandate.

WHY THIS PAYER IS NOT ONE ALREADY TESTED. Two payers carry every family in this ledger. (a) The FUNDING payer -- H0002, H0006, H0007, H0016 -- is identified by a coupon paid every eight hours. This basket pays us no coupon and its rebalance is not a settlement event; nothing in this rule reads panel.funding_rate, and the funding the evaluator charges is a cost of holding, never an input to a decision. (b) The LIQUIDATED holder of section 7b -- H0017 and H0019, 162 rows -- is past maintenance margin and is closed by the venue's risk engine at a price and a moment neither of them chose. This basket is solvent throughout. Nothing about its margin is breached when it trades; it trades because a ratio drifted, and it would still trade in a market with no liquidations in it at all.

WHAT THIS RULE CANNOT SEPARATE, SAID BEFORE ANY NUMBER EXISTS. Both payers buy after a rise. A liquidated short must buy and a levered-long basket must buy, so the SIGN of the flow does not tell them apart, and price alone never will. I am not claiming this hypothesis identifies which of them moved a bar. The discriminating prediction is not the sign but the DURATION over which the displacement is measured, and that is the whole content of the axis below: a mandate restored while the drift is fresh predicts an edge read against a recent reference, whereas an edge read against a fortnight or a month is a trend, and a trend has no forced payer in it. The clause that fires on that is 5, and it can close this family even when clause 1 is met.

WHY THE AXIS IS lookback_days, AND WHY IT HAS NEVER BEEN ENUMERATED. Every CCI row this project holds -- H0017's 90 and H0019's 72, 162 in total -- was run at lookback_days = 5.0. lookback_days is the CCI period expressed as a DURATION, so one registered value means the same window on every timeframe. H0017 therefore varied timeframe_hours across five levels while every one of them measured the SAME five-day displacement at five sampling resolutions, and H0019 varied the strength and the resolution of a filter over a fast leg whose window was again five days. The axis that carries the mechanism's own timescale has exactly one point in the entire ledger, and both families closed on SPIKE along axes that only re-sample it.

WHY THIS IS NOT A FINER GRID, WHICH I RAISE AGAINST MYSELF FIRST. H0020 and H0021 were killed on this ground hours ago and I take the adversary's own criterion as written: take_profit was killed because it "is an existing numeric field of SignalTrialConfig read as an exit cap in orc/eval/signal.py, not the signal's state variable, entry, side or exit arrays". lookback_days IS the state variable. CCI is the typical price minus its mean over n, divided by 0.015 times its mean absolute deviation over n; n is not a threshold applied to a signal, it is the definition of the signal, and moving it rebuilds the entry array, the side array and the exit array together. A finer grid is more levels on an axis already enumerated -- that is what killed H0009 over H0007, and what killed H0020 and H0021 over H0017. This is an axis with one recorded level and five proposed ones.

WHY BOTH ARMS OF THE DUEL RUN. Section 7b: continuation is cci_breakout, relaxation is cci_reversion, "they cannot both be right at one horizon, and that disagreement is the test neither shape is alone". H0017 resolved that duel at ONE duration and recorded reversion at calmar > 0 on 0 of 9 symbols at every timeframe. Whether that is a property of relaxation or a property of a five-day window is precisely what this axis is for. Running the continuation arm alone would leave a positive result unable to distinguish "a mandated flow at a definite timescale" from "any rule reads this window well", which is the distinction the hypothesis exists to make.

WHY cci_mtf IS NOT IN THIS HYPOTHESIS. Read from the rule rather than from the name, as H0019's claim records it: cci_mtf enters AGAINST the permitted side -- `entry[up & (base <= -enter_level)] = LONG` -- which is a pullback, that is, relaxation under a regime permission. The mandate named here predicts continuation, so cci_mtf is the wrong function for this payer and adding it would be width with no question attached.

WHAT I CHANGED FROM H0017's FIXED BLOCK, INCLUDING THE CHANGE THAT COSTS ME AN ANCHOR. max_hold_days is null here where H0017 fixed 5.0. A five-day cap does not bind on a one-day window and binds hard on a twenty-day one, so carrying it would handicap the long end of the very axis clause 5 reads, and would bias the surface toward the answer this hypothesis predicts. I would rather lose the anchor than pre-load the test: removing the cap costs the exact replication of H0017's timeframe = 4h cells that the lookback_days = 5.0 column would otherwise have been, and no clause below reads H0017's numbers in any case, since H0018 was killed for a clause that depended on another family's payload. With the cap gone every cell exits on its own indicator, the stop, or a liquidation, which is what "exits on its own signal" means on Track B. Everything else is H0017's fixed block unchanged: timeframe_hours 4.0 (the candle the owner named), enter_level 100.0 and exit_level 50.0 (the same hysteresis, so the axis is the only thing that differs between cells), leverage 1.0 (KT-2 closed leverage above 1x and nothing here reopens it), stop_loss 0.25 as a tail bound far outside what the entry reads rather than as the rule's exit, capital 10000.0, clock "1h", and costs at the project defaults of 4.5 bps taker plus 1.0 bps slippage, 11 bps a round trip, charged inside every number recorded.

THE LEVELS, AND WHY THEY ARE LIVE. On the 4-hour candle the five windows are 6, 12, 30, 60 and 120 candles respectively. None is below six observations, so the mean absolute deviation in the denominator is never taken over a handful of points -- the ground on which H0019 dropped a 72-hour filter leg. The longest costs 20 days of warm-up out of roughly four and a half years of development data. 5.0 is on the grid as the axis's midpoint and as the only window the ledger has ever recorded, so the four new levels are read against a known point rather than against nothing.

WHAT THIS PROBE CANNOT SEE. (1) BLVT net asset value, assets under management, target leverage, basket composition and rebalance timestamps are not in this archive -- the scout line says so itself -- so the flow is not measured. A displaced price is evidence of flow and not a measurement of it, and ordinary aggressive trading displaces price too. (2) Which of the nine symbols ever carried a leveraged token is not in this archive either, so the cross-sectional control the scout line names, "concentrated in symbols represented by Binance Leveraged Tokens", cannot be built; the universe is the project's standard nine and carries no such control. (3) Whether and when the product was withdrawn is not dated anywhere I may read. If it was withdrawn inside the development window, the payer's flow is absent for part of it, which would show up as instability across symbols rather than as a clean fail, and I would not be able to tell the two apart. (4) "Abnormally high minute volume" is the other half of the scout line's observable and no rule in this evaluator reads volume. (5) enter_level is fixed at 100.0, so the +-200 extreme is untested here; readings past 200 are a SUBSET of what this enters on, so a FAIL here is a FAIL at the band with the extreme diluted into it and never a FAIL at the extreme. (6) The rule takes both sides symmetrically and no field of SignalTrialConfig restricts it to the buy side, so the asymmetry that would distinguish a forced buyer from a forced seller stays untested, exactly as it did in H0019.

WHAT THE NOTEBOOK HOLDS THAT THIS EVALUATOR CANNOT RUN, SINCE THAT IS ALSO A RESULT. The highest-confidence unused lines are calendar-driven -- quarterly delivery at a published index average inside the 07:00-08:00 UTC hour of the last Friday of a quarter (line 0), margin-tier tightening at a stated timestamp (line 1), borrow-suspension and margin-delisting deadlines (line 32), network suspension windows (line 19). Every one of them has an observable that lives in bars this project holds, and not one of them is expressible: SignalTrialConfig has no calendar field, no time-of-day field and no event table, so a rule keyed to a published minute expands to a TypeError. Lines 6, 15, 27 and 28 are reachable only at minute resolution or at cross-symbol simultaneity, and the clock here is hourly and single-symbol. That is why this proposal takes line 10: it is the only high-confidence payer in the notebook whose observable is a same-signed price displacement at an hours-to-days scale, which is the one thing this evaluator can express.

THE STOP CONDITION, HONESTLY. The owner's stop condition is a Calmar of at least 4.0 and I do not claim this shape reaches it. What is recorded is two CCI surfaces sitting near zero with single-symbol peaks at 3.006 (DOGEUSDT, H0017) and 1.579 (AVAXUSDT, H0019), and I argue from neither: both are SPIKE and both families closed on that clause. The narrower claim that justifies 90 rows is this. Both closures fired along axes that re-sample a displacement whose duration was never moved, so "the surface is a corner" has a candidate cause that has never been tested. If the surface is smooth along duration and peaks at the short end, that is a different object from what is recorded, and it earns a second registration. If it spikes along duration too, then the family the owner named is exhausted in the last direction this evaluator can express and closes for good. Both outcomes are map entries; the second is worth 90 rows precisely because it ends the family rather than leaving it open by omission.

COST. 2 rules x 5 windows = 10 cells over 9 symbols = 90 configurations. That is inside the 96-configuration probe ceiling, is the identical cost H0017 paid, and is 1.28 % of the 7,010 trials recorded at run 324595c30eb4. The rule pairing has zero rows in the ledger at any window other than 5.0 days.
proposal.kill_condition:
NOTATION AND FROZEN COUNTING RULES. Nine symbols s. Ten cells (r, n), with r in {cci_breakout, cci_reversion} and n in {1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0} days. C(s, r, n) is the recorded `calmar`. "The best cell" of a symbol means the cell the surface itself records as that symbol's best, which on Track B is the maximum recorded `calmar`; on an exact tie, the smaller n, and then cci_breakout. That selection rule is frozen here because H0018 was killed for leaving "the best cell" undefined across symbols. At the best cell the surface records `shape`, `independent_paths_best` (which on Track B is n_trades) and `n_liquidations_best`, and clauses 2, 3, 4 and 5 read only those. A cell that does not record at all -- run_signal_trial raising UnsupportedConfig('no_trades_fired') -- counts as FAILING every clause it appears in and never as passing one. No clause reads `gross_collected`, a cost-stressed value, a PBO, or any number belonging to another hypothesis, because each of those was recorded unevaluable at some earlier closure and an unrun check is not a check that passed. Every threshold below is frozen now, before any of these 90 configurations has been run.

1. NO EDGE. Closed if no single cell (r, n) reaches C > 0 on at least 5 of the 9 symbols. This is deliberately the identical bar, on the identical nine-symbol universe, that H0002, H0006, H0017 and H0019 were graded against, so this family cannot be graded on an easier scale than the ones it follows.

2. RUIN. Closed if `n_liquidations_best` is above 0 on any of the 9 symbols. At leverage 1.0 behind a 0.25 stop a liquidation should be unreachable, and if one is recorded the Calmar is describing how close to ruin the shape ran. KT-2 closed that direction already and this family does not get to reopen it by accident.

3. TOO THIN TO BE AN EXPERIMENT. Closed if `independent_paths_best` is below 20 on 5 or more of the 9 symbols. On Track B the effective independent-path count IS the trade count, and a curve made of a handful of episodes is a handful of experiments however it looks. This floor is live rather than decorative: with max_hold_days null, a 20-day window on a 4-hour candle both enters rarely and holds long, so if the best cells cluster at the long end the count is what will say so.

4. SPIKE. Closed if the recorded shape of the best cell is SPIKE on 5 or more of the 9 symbols. This clause is word-for-word H0017's and H0019's, and it is the clause that closed both -- 7 of 9 and 8 of 9. lookback_days carries five ordinal numeric levels precisely so the diagnostic has a step either side of the best cell to read; H0006 spent 72 configurations on all-binary axes and closed with the shape column reading '?' on every symbol.

5. THE TIMESCALE IS NOT THE PAYER'S. Closed if the best cell's `lookback_days` is 10.0 or 20.0 on 5 or more of the 9 symbols. A leverage mandate is restored against the exposure the basket carried days ago, not weeks ago, so the displacement this hypothesis names is one measured against a recent reference. A fortnight-long or month-long window is reading a trend, and a trend has no forced payer in it -- the mechanism would then be wrong even where clause 1 is met, which is why this clause can close the family on its own. Calibration, stated before the numbers: under a flat surface each of the five levels wins 1.8 of the 9 symbols, so the two long levels together win 3.6 by chance and a threshold of 5 is a real majority above chance rather than a coin flip. 5.0 days is deliberately NOT on the closing side: it is the axis's midpoint and the only window the ledger has ever recorded, and making the reference level a closing level would fire this clause on the very point the axis is read against.

6. THE DUEL DOES NOT RESOLVE. Closed if there exists an n for which BOTH (cci_breakout, n) and (cci_reversion, n) reach C > 0 on 5 or more of the 9 symbols. Section 7b is explicit that continuation and relaxation cannot both be right at one horizon. If both are paid at the same window, the indicator is being paid for taking a position of either sign in dispersion, which is a property of the surface and not a payer, and the mechanism named in the claim is not what produced it.

WHAT SURVIVAL WOULD REQUIRE, on the record before the numbers and not softenable afterwards: one single cell (r, n) with C > 0 on at least 5 of the 9 symbols; no liquidation recorded at any symbol's best cell; at least 5 symbols whose best cell fired 20 trades or more; a shape that is not SPIKE on a majority; a best window of 1.0, 2.0 or 5.0 days on a majority; and no window at which both arms clear the 5-of-9 bar. Only then may a second registration under a new id enumerate the +-200 extreme, the exit hysteresis, the candle resolutions and the hold cap this probe fixed. A FAIL on any clause above is a publishable result and, since it fires along the last axis of the CCI family the evaluator can express, it closes that family rather than leaving it open by omission.

verdict.reason: [codex] This is a finer grid over the already-registered CCI rule forms: it changes only `lookback_days`, a parameter of `cci_breakout` and `cci_reversion`, while the alleged BLVT flow is neither measured nor encoded as a different rule shape. Renaming the payer cannot reopen the CCI family established in section 7b.
